title: Operational Bridgebook: Responder Handoffs, Communications, and Readiness
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary:
This document (the ‘Operational Bridgebook’) codifies the on-call lifecycle for Redwood Inference: how incidents are triaged, how responders hand over the operational 'bridge' between shifts, runbook steps for common high-impact failure modes, how we run game days to validate readiness, and the approved templates for status page and customer-facing communications. The aim is to reduce cognitive load during incidents, shorten time-to-restoration, and standardize learning capture.

Scope:
- Applies to all services in the public inference control plane, dedicated fleet control plane, and private deployment support teams.
- Includes SREs, runtime engineers, support leads, and customer success engineers who may author or send customer communications.
- Excludes purely product feature bug triage that does not impact service availability or SLOs.

Incident lifecycle (high level):
1) Signal detection and enrichment
   - Automated alerting from Prometheus/Alertmanager, tracing-based anomaly detectors, or customer reports via support.
   - On alert: the first responder (FR) checks the alert dashboard and the service status tag within 5 minutes.
2) Triage and classification (first 15 minutes)
   - Determine impact: latency SLO % deviation, error rate increase, or total outage.
   - Classify severity: Sev-1 (critical customer-impact, multi-region outage), Sev-2 (localized/limited impact), Sev-3 (degraded non-critical).
3) Contain and mitigate
   - Execute targeted runbooks (examples below). If no runbook exists, proceed with containment play: scale, circuit-break, route-around.
4) Restore and stabilize
   - Gradual ramp down mitigations, confirm metrics return to baseline for two successive 5-minute windows.
5) Customer comms and status page
   - Draft initial public message within 30 minutes for Sev-1/Sev-2. Use templates in the Communications section.
6) Post-incident review and close
   - Complete postmortem within 5 business days for Sev-1/Sev-2 and 10 business days for Sev-3.

Responder roles and responsibilities:
- First Responder (FR): owned by on-call engineer. Immediate triage and runbook execution.
- Incident Lead (IL): coordinates across teams, assigns action owners, and approves customer messaging.
- SRE Coordinator (SRE-C): ensures runbook access, paging cadence, and escalation to infra.
- Customer Success Liaison (CSL): drafts customer-specific follow-ups for impacted accounts.
- Communications Owner (CO): publishes status page updates and external notices.

Operational Bridge Handover Checklist (must be completed during every shift transfer):
- Handover preamble: summary of outstanding incidents, actions in progress, and outstanding watch windows (one short paragraph).
- State snapshot: current active incidents (IDs), impact level, mitigation in place, metric links (CPU, latency p50/p95/p99, error rate), and timeline of last 2 events.
- Tickets and actions: list of open runbook steps with owner and ETA.
- Escalation status: who has been paged and next escalation tier contact details.
- Sensitive notes: any customer-sensitive constraints, legal/contractual hold points, or embargoed fixes.
- Acceptance: incoming on-call acknowledges handover, repeats back the critical mitigation and ETA, and records a single-line confirmation in the shift log.

Handover ‘script’ (example):
1. Outgoing: "We have active incident #INC-2026-1032, Sev-2, inferred autoscaler regression affecting us-east-1 only. Autoscaling currently disabled; emergency scale-up requested and in progress (ETA 14m). P50 up from 120ms to 540ms, errors at 2.3%. Next action: IL to monitor scale events and revert autoscaler when stable."
2. Incoming: "Acknowledged. I see the scale event in progress — I will watch the autoscaler logs and metrics, and call IL at 14m if not complete. Adding myself as owner in the incident."

Fast Restoration Runbook: High tail latency on inference nodes
Purpose: Reduce service-wide p99 latency spikes without lasting customer regressions.
Preconditions: Observation of p99 > 1.5x SLO for two consecutive 5-minute windows, or large error spike.
Steps:
1) Confirm service and region scope (dashboard link). Record timestamps and sample traces.
2) Check for hot shards: run `kubectl get pods -l app=inference -n runtime -o wide` and compare CPU/GPU utilization.
3) If one or more nodes show >85% GPU utilization, enable temporary pod-level request throttling: patch the deployment to add evictions = false and set pod disruption budget to 0.
4) If autoscaler misbehaviour suspected, temporarily disable horizontal autoscaler and scale replicas to calculated target: `kubectl scale deployment inference --replicas N -n runtime` (N = current + 30%).
5) If latency persists, trigger routing fallback to lighter quantized model variant (routing policy id: rp-quant-fallback-1). Notify IL.
6) Monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rate for 10 minutes; if stable for two windows, begin rollback of temporary changes and document actions.
7) If rollback fails, escalate to infra and open a support request for driver/kernel-level investigation.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- Within 15 minutes: page team on-call.
- At 30 minutes: page IL and SRE Coordinator.
- At 60 minutes: page infra-oncall and product-owner on call.
- At 120 minutes: page exec pager and Customer Success Director (for high customer impact).

SLOs and alert thresholds (table):
| Service | SLO (p99) | Alert threshold | Pager severity |
| Inference API (hosted) | <= 800ms | p99 > 1.5x SLO for 5m | Sev-2 |
| Embeddings API | <= 1200ms | p99 > 1.5x SLO for 5m | Sev-2 |
| Control plane (API) | 99.95% availability monthly | 0.05% drop in availability | Sev-1 |

Game day play: Multi-region degraded routing (90m exercise)
Objective: Test automated routing fallbacks, cross-region capacity ramp, and customer comms automation.
Prereqs: staging cleanup, Canary models loaded in backup regions, and a simulated load generator.
Schedule:
- 00:00–00:10: Inject routing rule to mark us-west-2 as degraded.
- 00:10–00:30: Simulate 3x traffic to us-east-1. Verify autoscale and latency SLOs.
- 00:30–00:45: Force one control-plane instance restart and validate fallback to dedicated failover model.
- 00:45–01:20: Run customer comms drill: draft and publish status update, targeted customer notices via templated emails.
Post-game-day: 3-day deferred debrief and a 2-week follow-up for runbook improvements.

Status page and customer communications (approved templates)
- Public status page timeline (short):
  - Title: "Degraded latency for inference API (region: us-east-1)"
  - Impact: "Some customers may experience increased latency or transient errors while we failover traffic."
  - Current status: "Investigating / Mitigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved" (choose one)
  - Next update: timestamp +30m or milestone change
  - Technical summary: single short paragraph, no internal debugging detail.

- External customer email template (for Sev-1 / major account impact):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident update: [Short summary]
  Body: Hello [Customer name],

  We are investigating an issue impacting the Redwood Inference API in [region]. Impact: customers may experience higher latency or failed requests. What we have done: performed routing failover to backup region and are scaling capacity. What you can expect: next update within 30 minutes; we will provide a full post-incident report within 5 business days. If this issue is causing critical customer impact for you, please reply and we will prioritize your ticket.

  Regards,
  Redwood Inference Operations Team

- In-product banner text (short): "We are investigating elevated latency for inference requests in [region]. We expect a resolution within ~30–60 minutes."

Postmortem & learning capture (template and expectations):
- Required fields for Sev-1/Sev-2 postmortem: summary, timeline of events (minute granularity first hour), root cause hypothesis, contributing factors, detection delta, total time-to-restore, customer impact (list of accounts), remediation actions, corrective actions owner + ETA, and follow-up verification plan.
- Blamelessness: focus on system gaps and process improvements. Do not name individuals as causes.
- Distribution: publish to Confluence and link to incident in the on-call shift log. For Sev-1 include a 15-minute stakeholder sync and an executive summary for leadership.

Shift logging and metrics capture (minimum requirements):
- Every shift must append a single-line entry to the shared shift log with the following CSV fields: date,time,shift-owner,active-incidents,highest-severity,notable-actions.
- Incident metric snapshots: attach a link to the time-series graph and a sample trace for key services within the incident ticket.

Operational tooling links (example list):
- Alerts dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/alerts
- Incident tracker: https://jira.redwood.internal/secure/Dashboard.jspa
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.internal/manage
- Runbook library (consolidated): https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/ops/Runbook+Index

Appendix A — Quick Slack templates (use channel #ops-incidents and private incident channels):
- Initial page (short): `:rotating_light: [INC-ID] Detected elevated p99 for inference-api in us-east-1. FR on-call: @oncall-name. Triage in progress.`
- Update after mitigation: `:white_check_mark: [INC-ID] Routing fallback to quantized model applied. p99 improving from 1.8s -> 720ms. Monitoring.`
- Customer message ready: `@cs-team External message drafted for affected accounts, ready to send on IL approval.`

Appendix B — Contact matrix (short):
- On-call infra pager: infra-oncall@redwood.internal
- Exec pager: exec-pager@redwood.internal
- Customer Success Director: cynthia.lowe@redwood.com

Governance and continuous improvement:
- Runbook ownership review: every runbook must have an owner and a quarterly review date. The oncall-and-incident-response team will run a quarterly sweep and retire or update stale runbooks.
- Game day cadence: at least one cross-team game day per quarter and one targeted runbook drill per team every month.
- Metrics for readiness: mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) target < 3 minutes, mean time to restore (MTTR) target for Sev-1 < 45 minutes.

Related pages and resources:
- Link to Runbook Index, Incident Postmortem template, and Oncall Roster (see Runbook Index).
